'''Scott D. Emr''' (born February 8, 1954) is an American [[cell biology|cell biologist]] and the founding and current Director of the [[Weill Institute for Cell and Molecular Biology]] at [[Cornell University]], where he is also a [[Frank H.T. Rhodes]] Class of 1956 Professor at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics.<ref name="emrlab">{{cite web |title=The Emr Lab |url=https://emr.wicmb.cornell.edu/ |publisher=Cornell University |access-date=November 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211108222944/https://emr.wicmb.cornell.edu/ |archive-date=November 8, 2021}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Emr was born in [[Jersey City, New Jersey|Jersey City]]<ref name="shaw"/> and grew up in [[Fort Lee, New Jersey]]. His father was a manager of a manufacturing company. He has a sister and two brothers.<ref name="autobiography"/>

The 1960s documentary ''[[The Undersea World of Jacques Cousteau]]'' prompted him to pick a [[university]] with a strong [[oceanography]] program, starting in 1972 at the [[University of Rhode Island]] as a [[biology]] major. He became interested in [[genetics]] during his [[Undergraduate education|undergraduate]] years.<ref name="autobiography"/> He started his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1976 at the Department of Microbiology and Molecular Genetics at [[Harvard University]], working under [[Thomas Silhavy]] and [[Jon Beckwith|Jonathan Beckwith]] and graduating in 1981.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="autobiography"/>

== Career ==
Emr began his career at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as a [[Miller Institute]] Fellow<ref>{{cite web |title=All Miller Fellows: By Name |url=https://miller.berkeley.edu/fellowship/members/all-mf-by-name |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |access-date=November 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211112154753/https://miller.berkeley.edu/fellowship/members/all-mf-by-name |archive-date=November 12, 2021}}</ref> and a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at [[Randy Schekman]]'s group.<ref name="autobiography"/> He moved to the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1983, becoming an [[assistant professor|assistant]], and later [[associate professor]], at the Division of Biology.<ref name="bio"/>

[[George Emil Palade]] recruited Emr to the [[University of California, San Diego]] in 1991,<ref name="autobiography"/> where he stayed as a Distinguished Professor at the Department of Cellular and Molecular  Medicine and, at the same time, an investigator at the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Scott D. Emr, PhD |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/scott-d-emr |publisher=[[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] |access-date=November 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211116162032/https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/scott-d-emr |archive-date=November 16, 2021}}</ref> He left for [[Cornell University]] in 2007 when he was appointed as the founding director of the Institute of Cell and Molecular Biology (later renamed to [[Weill Institute for Cell and Molecular Biology]] after a donation from Joan and [[Sanford I. Weill]])<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramanujan |first1=Krishna |title=Institute for Cell and Molecular Biology benefits from $25 million gift from the Weills |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2007/06/weill-gift-will-benefit-institute-cell-and-molecular-biology |access-date=November 15, 2021 |work=[[Cornell Chronicle]] |date=June 13, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211115154833/https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2007/06/weill-gift-will-benefit-institute-cell-and-molecular-biology |archive-date=November 15, 2021}}</ref> and a [[Frank H.T. Rhodes]] Class of 1956 Professor at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics.<ref name="bio"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramanujan |first1=Krishna |title=A major hire to advance and extend life sciences at Cornell |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2006/05/emrs-hire-key-restructuring-life-sciences-cornell |date=May 24, 2006 |access-date=November 16, 2021 |work=Cornell Chronicle |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211116155907/https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2006/05/emrs-hire-key-restructuring-life-sciences-cornell |archive-date=November 16, 2021}}</ref>

Academically, Emr serves on the editorial boards of several scientific journals, including (as of 2021) ''[[mBio]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=mBio Board of Editors |url=https://journals.asm.org/journal/mbio/board-editors |publisher=[[mBio]] |archive-date=November 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119151754/https://journals.asm.org/journal/mbio/board-editors |access-date=November 19, 2021}}</ref> ''[[Journal of Cell Biology]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://rupress.org/jcb/pages/editors-and-staff |publisher=[[Journal of Cell Biology]] |access-date=November 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814180357/https://rupress.org/jcb/pages/editors-and-staff |archive-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref> ''[[Trends (journals)|Trends in Cell Biology]]'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Advisory board |url=https://www.cell.com/trends/cell-biology/advisory-board |publisher=[[Trends (journals)|Trends in Cell Biology]] |access-date=November 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123151740/https://www.cell.com/trends/cell-biology/advisory-board |archive-date=November 23, 2021}}</ref> and ''[[Current Opinion in Cell Biology]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/current-opinion-in-cell-biology/editorial-board |publisher=[[Current Opinion in Cell Biology]] |access-date=November 23, 2021 |archive-date=November 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123152039/https://www.journals.elsevier.com/current-opinion-in-cell-biology/editorial-board}}</ref>

== Research ==
Emr's research focuses on the regulation of [[membrane vesicle trafficking]] pathways. His lab's study of the [[ESCRT]] (endosomal sorting complexes required for transport) complexes earned him a [[Shaw Prize]] in Life Science and Medicine.<ref>{{cite press release |date=June 1, 2021 |title=Press Release |url=https://www.shawprize.org/prizes-and-laureates/life-science-and-medicine/2021/press-release |publisher=The Shaw Prize Foundation |access-date=November 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211124144513/https://www.shawprize.org/prizes-and-laureates/life-science-and-medicine/2021/press-release |archive-date=November 24, 2021}}</ref> ESCRTs are required for the degradation of [[membrane protein]] at the [[lysosome]], a late step in [[cytokinesis]], and the budding and release of [[HIV|human immunodeficiency virus]] (HIV).<ref name="bio"/><ref name="emrlab"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Katzmann |first1=David J. |last2=Babst |first2=Markus |last3=Emr |first3=Scott D. |title=Ubiquitin-Dependent Sorting into the Multivesicular Body Pathway Requires the Function of a Conserved Endosomal Protein Sorting Complex, ESCRT-I |journal=[[Cell (journal)|Cell]] |date=2001 |volume=106 |issue=2 |pages=145–155 |doi=10.1016/S0092-8674(01)00434-2 |pmid=11511343 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Banjade |first1=Sudeep |last2=Tsang |first2=Shaogeng |last3=Shah |first3=Yousuf H |last4=Emr |first4=Scott D |title=Electrostatic lateral interactions drive ESCRT-III heteropolymer assembly |journal=[[eLife]] |date=2019 |volume=8 |article-number=e46207 |doi=10.7554/eLife.46207 |pmid=31246173 |pmc=6663469 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

His other research interests include [[lipid signaling]] (especially a group of lipids known as [[Phosphatidylinositol#Phosphoinositides|phosphatidylinositol phosphates]]),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Burd |first1=Christopher G |last2=Emr |first2=Scott D |title=Phosphatidylinositol(3)-phosphate signaling mediated by specific binding to RING FYVE domains |journal=[[Molecular Cell]] |date=1998 |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=157–162 |doi=10.1016/S1097-2765(00)80125-2 |pmid=9702203 |doi-access=free }}</ref> [[protein]] [[Intracellular transport|transport in cells]] by [[Vesicle (biology and chemistry)|vesicles]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Suzuki |first1=Sho W. |last2=Emr |first2=Scott D. |title=Membrane protein recycling from the vacuole/lysosome membrane |journal=[[Journal of Cell Biology]] |date=2018 |volume=217 |issue=5 |pages=1623–1632 |doi=10.1083/jcb.201709162 |pmid=29511122 |url=https://rupress.org/jcb/article/217/5/1623/38909/Membrane-protein-recycling-from-the-vacuole |access-date=November 29, 2021 |pmc=5940307 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211129153251/https://rupress.org/jcb/article/217/5/1623/38909/Membrane-protein-recycling-from-the-vacuole |archive-date=November 29, 2021}}</ref> and the role of [[arrestin]] and [[Ubiquitin#Ubiquitylation|ubiquitylation]] in the degradation of membrane proteins.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="emrlab"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lin |first1=Charles H. |last2=MacGurn |first2=Jason A. |last3=Chu |first3=Tony |last4=Stefan |first4=Christopher J. |last5=Emr |first5=Scott D. |title=Arrestin-related ubiquitin-ligase adaptors regulate endocytosis and protein turnover at the cell surface |journal=Cell |date=2008 |volume=135 |issue=4 |pages=714–725 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2008.09.025 |pmid=18976803 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Emr met his wife Michelle in his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year at university. She was also in her third year, majoring in [[music]] and [[Early childhood education|early education]]. They married three years later when Emr was pursuing his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]]. As of 2021, their daughter Bryanna is a [[pediatric surgery|pediatric surgeon]] in [[Pittsburgh]], and their son Kevin is an [[anesthesiology|anesthesiologist]] in [[Albany, New York]].<ref name="autobiography"/>
